physicalNotes: No radius or mass of MoM-z14 is recorded here: its package frames it at 14,624 pc (object.json worldFrame.bodyRadiusM), half the short side of its picture at its distance, a presentation value.

sources.position: Naidu et al. (2025), A Cosmic Miracle: A Remarkably Luminous Galaxy at z = 14.44 Confirmed with JWST, Open Journal of Astrophysics; position as SIMBAD records it from the paper (https://arxiv.org/abs/2505.11263); RA 150.0933255°, Dec 2.2731627° (SIMBAD, coordinate reference arXiv:2505.11263)
sources.distance: Comoving distance of the redshift z = 14.44 (Naidu et al. (2025), Open Journal of Astrophysics, arXiv:2505.11263) in the Planck 2018 cosmology: 10381694323.464087 pc, from Astropy 8.0.1 Planck18.comoving_distance (Planck Collaboration 2020, A&A 641, A6, https://arxiv.org/abs/1807.06209). The project's convention for objects placed by redshift (packages/bake/cli/prepare-catalogue-points.mts).
sources.properMotion: Zero: the object is held at its published position; no motion across the sky is applied.
sources.radialVelocity: c z for the redshift z = 14.44: the redshift written as a velocity, not a motion through space. Naidu et al. (2025), Open Journal of Astrophysics, arXiv:2505.11263 (https://arxiv.org/abs/2505.11263); abstract: z_spec = 14.44 +0.02 -0.02.
